12	version, and stops you from inventing APIs — match the installed versions and
13	follow the ecosystem catalog instead of guessing.

27	  the check. Do not repeatedly rebuild unchanged code.

32	needs. Do not guess from training data — the ecosystem has look-alike packages

63	   stopping at the first source that answers your question:**

72	      (e.g. `/llms/uikit/7/llms.txt` for `^7.2.1`). The major-line URL serves the
73	      latest minor of that major — it tracks the major but not the exact patch.
74	      Use it when LOCAL has no docs for the package.

77

101	1. **Implement using only the `@gravity-ui/*` packages chosen in Step 0 and
102	   confirmed installed in Step 1.** Import from those packages exactly — do
103	   not substitute look-alike libraries (MUI, Ant, plain `<input>`) and do not

105	   Follow the prop APIs from the docs you just read, not memory; if a prop
106	   you want is not documented, it does not exist — use the documented one, or
107	   ask the user.

110	   writing: typography variants, the flex contract, theming/ladders,
111	   `Button view`, `Icon data`. Per-component traps live in the package's own
112	   `dist/docs`.

115	   (typically `tsc --noEmit`; for monorepos, the workspace's typecheck script).
116	   Fix every error before reporting completion — a type error almost always
117	   means a wrong/invented prop, a wrong import path, or a version mismatch,
118	   which is precisely what Steps 0–1 were meant to prevent.

121	     in Step 1, trust the **installed version** (the typechecker), not the
122	     docs snapshot — the docs may be from a different minor. Re-ground: read
123	     the package's `dist/docs/INDEX.md` in `node_modules` for the exact
124	     installed types.
125	   - If the typecheck is unavailable (no TS in the project), say so
126	     explicitly and ask the user how they want to verify; do not silently
127	     skip verification.
128	   - **Escape hatch.** If the user explicitly waived verification ("just
129	     sketch it", "quick prototype", "no need to check"), you may skip the
130	     typecheck — but state this plainly in your reply: *"typecheck skipped by
131	     user request — code is not verified"*. Do not skip silently.
132	
133	## Hard rules
134	
135	- **`@gravity-ui/uikit` MUST be installed in every Gravity UI project.** It is
136	  the base component + design-token library every other `@gravity-ui/*` package
137	  builds on; without it components render unstyled. If `package.json` lacks it,
138	  stop and have the user install and configure it first (setup:
139	  `https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt`).
140	- **Read `package.json` before importing any `@gravity-ui/*` package.** Never
141	  assume a package is installed; never assume its major version.
142	- **Do not invent props or components.** Before using a component API you are
143	  not 100% sure of, check `rules/hallucination-traps.md` (ecosystem patterns)
144	  and the component's README in `dist/docs`. If still unsure, ask the user
145	  rather than guessing.
146	- **Never guess icon names** — they are hallucinated more often than not. To
147	  match an icon from a screenshot/photo/mock, run `scripts/icon-image-search.sh`
148	  (reverse image search). With only a description, look the name up on
149	  `gravity-ui.com/icons` or ask the user — do not invent one. Then pass it as an
150	  object (`<Icon data={CheckIcon} />`), never a string key. See
151	  `references/icons.md`.
152	- **Theming uses semantic `--g-*` tokens.** Never hardcode colors (`#fff`,
153	  `blue-500`); never hand-write `dark:` overrides. Full token tables live in
154	  `references/theming.md`; the cross-cutting traps (partial brand overrides,
155	  scoped vs nested `ThemeProvider`, controls on a brand background) live in
156	  `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
157	- **Required setup is package-specific** (style imports, `ThemeProvider`,
158	  peer-deps). It lives in each package's root README under "Required setup" —
159	  read it once per package, do not rely on memory.
160	
161	## What NOT to do
162	
163	These are the five most common ways agents break Gravity UI code. They are
164	already implied by the rules above; this section exists as an explicit
165	stop-sign. If you are about to do any of these, stop and re-ground.
166	
167	- **Do not substitute non-Gravity libraries.** No MUI, Ant Design, plain
168	  `<input>`/`<button>`, or look-alike component libs. Use the `@gravity-ui/*`
169	  package the task needs.
170	- **Do not invent component APIs or props.** If a prop is not in the docs you
171	  read in Step 1, it does not exist — do not write `variant=`, `color=`,
172	  `name=` (on `Icon`), or a `header-3` variant. Use the documented prop or
173	  ask the user. See `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
174	- **Do not use the `/llms/<pkg>/llms.txt` "latest" alias as a fallback.** It
175	  serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
176	  different API. The versioned online fallback is the major-line URL
177	  (`/llms/<pkg>/<major>/llms.txt`); below that, go LOCAL.
178	- **Do not partial-brand.** Setting only `--g-color-base-brand` leaves
179	  selection, focus, links and contrast on the default accent — a mismatched
180	  UI. Override the full brand token set, on each theme you support.
181	- **Do not override internal markup with `[class*='…']` / ID selectors.**
182	  That's written against one DOM structure and breaks silently when the
183	  component changes. Climb the customization ladder
184	  (global token → component CSS API → narrow flagged hack) before ever
185	  touching structure.
186	
187	## Deeper material — read on demand
188	
189	These files live alongside this SKILL.md and load only when relevant:
190	
191	- `references/package-routing.md` — offline snapshot of the ecosystem catalog
192	  (`gravity-ui.com/llms.txt`), refreshed each skill release. Used as the
193	  offline fallback in Step 0.
194	- `references/theming.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/theming.md`:
195	  `--g-*` token layers, `ThemeProvider`, branding, custom themes, scoped
196	  themes, `uikit-themer`. The bundled copy may lag — read
197	  `node_modules/@gravity-ui/uikit/build/docs/guides/theming.md` for the
198	  version-matched file.
199	- `references/layout.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/layout.md`:
200	  spacing scale (`--g-spacing-*`), `Flex`/`Box`, `Row`/`Col`/`Container`
201	  grid, breakpoints, `useLayoutContext`.
202	- `references/icons.md` — finding an icon by image
203	  (`scripts/icon-image-search.sh`) or on gravity-ui.com/icons; the
204	  object-vs-string rendering rule.
205	- `rules/hallucination-traps.md` — Incorrect/Correct pairs for the most
206	  commonly invented APIs: typography variants (`header-3..6` don't exist, no
207	  `Heading`), the flex contract (`min-width:0`, who shrinks), theming traps
208	  (partial brand overrides, scoped vs nested `ThemeProvider`, customization
209	  ladder), `Button view` not `variant`, `Icon data` not `name`. Per-component
210	  traps live in each package's `dist/docs`, not here.

8	## For AI agents
9	
10	A library for rendering whole web pages or page sections from declarative JSON/YAML config, using a set of ready-made, orderable blocks — reach for it to build marketing/landing pages, not general application UI.
11	
12	### When to use
13	
14	- Data-driven pages: render a `content` config of typed blocks with `PageConstructor` wrapped in `PageConstructorProvider`.
15	- Marketing, landing, and documentation pages assembled from prebuilt blocks (headers, media, cards, etc.).
16	- Server-side YFM processing of block text via the `@gravity-ui/page-constructor/server` utilities (`contentTransformer`, `fullTransform`).
17	- Reusing just the responsive grid (`Grid`/`Row`/`Col`) or `Navigation` component standalone.
18	
19	### When not to use
20	
21	- General application UI (buttons, forms, modals) — use [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit).
22	- Editing Markdown/YFM content — use [`@gravity-ui/markdown-editor`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/markdown-editor).
23	- App navigation shells (aside header) — use [`@gravity-ui/navigation`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/navigation); this package's `Navigation` is a page-level top nav.
24	
25	### Common pitfalls
26	
27	- **`PageConstructor` must be wrapped in `PageConstructorProvider`.** Rendering it bare breaks context (locale, theme, SSR, analytics).
28	- **The content prop is `content`, shaped `{blocks: [...]}`.** Each block object needs a `type` matching a known block plus its data fields; there is no `data`/`config` prop.
29	- **YFM in block text needs server processing.** Markdown-like fields render as plain text unless you run content through `contentTransformer`/`fullTransform` from `@gravity-ui/page-constructor/server`; `@diplodoc/transform` is a required peer dependency.
30	- **Import the SCSS styles.** Add `@gravity-ui/page-constructor/styles/styles.scss` (SCSS, not CSS); custom blocks import the same file to reuse mixins/variables.
31	- **Vite needs `vite-plugin-dynamic-import`.** Dynamic block imports fail under Vite without it.
32	- **The grid needs a global `box-sizing: border-box` reset.** The package does not ship one; without it the container padding overflows the viewport horizontally while typecheck and build stay green. Add `*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }` to the host app styles.
33	
34	## Install
35	
36	```shell
37	npm install @gravity-ui/page-constructor
38	```
39	
40	## Usage
41	
42	First, we need a React project and some kind of server. For example, you can create a React project using Vite and an Express server, or you can create Next.js application - it will have a client and server side at once.
43	
44	Install the required dependencies:
45	
46	```shell
47	npm install @gravity-ui/page-constructor @diplodoc/transform @gravity-ui/uikit
48	```
49	
50	Insert the `Page Constructor` to the page. To work correctly, it must be wrapped in a `PageConstructorProvider`:
51	
52	```tsx
53	import {PageConstructor, PageConstructorProvider} from '@gravity-ui/page-constructor';
54	import '@gravity-ui/page-constructor/styles/styles.scss';
55	
56	const App = () => {
57	  const content = {
58	    blocks: [
59	      {
60	        type: 'header-block',
61	        title: 'Hello world',
62	        background: {color: '#f0f0f0'},
63	        description:
64	          '**Congratulations!** Have you built a [page-constructor](https://github.com/gravity-ui/page-constructor) into your website',
65	      },
66	    ],
67	  };
68	
69	  return (
70	    <PageConstructorProvider>
71	      <PageConstructor content={content} />
72	    </PageConstructorProvider>
73	  );
74	};
75	
76	export default App;
77	```
78	
79	This was the simplest example of a connection. In order for YFM markup to work, you need to process content on the server and receive it on the client.
80	
81	If your server is a separate application, then you need to install page-constructor:
82	
83	```shell
84	npm install @gravity-ui/page-constructor
85	```
86	
87	To process YFM in all base blocks, call the `contentTransformer` and pass the content and options there:
88	
89	```ts
90	const express = require('express');
91	const app = express();
92	const {contentTransformer} = require('@gravity-ui/page-constructor/server');
93	
94	const content = {
95	  blocks: [
96	    {
97	      type: 'header-block',
98	      title: 'Hello world',
99	      background: {color: '#f0f0f0'},
100	      description:
101	        '**Congratulations!** Have you built a [page-constructor](https://github.com/gravity-ui/page-constructor) into your website',
102	    },
103	  ],
104	};
105	
106	app.get('/content', (req, res) => {
107	  res.send({content: contentTransformer({content, options: {lang: 'en'}})});
108	});
109	
110	app.listen(3000);
111	```
112	
113	On the client, add an endpoint call to receive content:
114	
115	```tsx
116	import {PageConstructor, PageConstructorProvider} from '@gravity-ui/page-constructor';
117	import '@gravity-ui/page-constructor/styles/styles.scss';
118	import {useEffect, useState} from 'react';
119	
120	const App = () => {
121	  const [content, setContent] = useState();
122	
123	  useEffect(() => {
124	    (async () => {
125	      const response = await fetch('http://localhost:3000/content').then((r) => r.json());
126	      setContent(response.content);
127	    })();
128	  }, []);
129	
130	  return (
131	    <PageConstructorProvider>
132	      <PageConstructor content={content} />
133	    </PageConstructorProvider>
134	  );
135	};
136	
137	export default App;
138	```

141	
142	To start a new project, you can use the [ready-made template on Next.js ](https://github.com/gravity-ui/page-constructor-website-template) which we have prepared.

145	
146	[Page Constructor Builder](https://github.com/gravity-ui/page-constructor-builder) - command-line utility for building static pages from YAML configurations using the @gravity-ui/page-constructor

148	## Guides
149	
150	- [Data preparation](./guides/data-preparation.md) — This chapter provides documentaion for server utilities for transforming content, including Yandex Flavored Markdown (YFM) to HTML conversion and text processing. Key features include:
151	- [Подготовка данных](./guides/data-preparation-ru.md) — Документацию по серверным утилитам для преобразования контента, включая конвертацию Yandex Flavored Markdown (YFM) в HTML и обработку текста. Основные возможности:
152	
153	## Blocks
154	
155	- [Banner](./blocks/Banner.md) — Renders a compact promotional card with a title, subtitle, an optional background image or color, and a single call-to-action button. Use it to highlight a feature, announce a release, or drive traffic to a landing page from anywhere in the page flow.
156	- [CardLayout](./blocks/CardLayout.md) — Renders a responsive grid of arbitrary cards (children) with an optional header and a decorative background image. Use it whenever you need to lay out a homogeneous set of cards — basic, image, background, price, or layout-item — in a row that adapts to the viewport.
157	- [Companies](./blocks/Companies.md) — Renders a heading with a logo strip — a set of responsive images (desktop / tablet / mobile) shown beneath an optional title and description. Use it for "trusted by" or "powered by" logo rows that must adapt per device and theme.
158	- [ContentLayout](./blocks/ContentLayout.md) — Renders a single-column content section (title, body text, optional list, links, and buttons) paired with an optional list of downloadable files and a background. 159	- [ExtendedFeatures](./blocks/ExtendedFeatures.md) — Renders a responsive grid of feature cards, each with an icon, title, text, an optional label (New / Preview), and an optional link. Use it to present a list of product features, capabilities, or benefits in a compact, icon-driven layout.
160	- [FilterBlock](./blocks/FilterBlock.md) — Renders a set of cards grouped by tags, with a row of toggle buttons that lets the visitor filter the visible cards by tag. Use it to present a catalog of cards (articles, features, products) that the user can narrow down without leaving the page.
161	- [FoldableList](./blocks/FoldableList.md) — Renders a two-column block: a content panel on the left (title, text, links, buttons) and a list of collapsible items on the right, each with its own title, YFM text, and optional link. Use it for FAQ-style or specification pages where each row expands to reveal more detail.
162	- [Footer](./blocks/Footer.md) — A configurable page footer assembled from optional floors: navigation columns, contacts (social icons), disclaimer, copyright (legal links, language switcher, logo), and an attribution strip.
163	- [Form](./blocks/Form.md) — A two-column block that renders a third-party form (Yandex Forms or HubSpot) alongside optional YFM text content, with a configurable layout direction and background.
164	- [Header](./blocks/Header.md) — Renders a full-width page header with a title, optional overtitle/description, call-to-action buttons, breadcrumbs, and an optional media asset (image, video, or video iframe) positioned to the right or centered. Use it as the primary hero/landing block at the top of a page.
165	- [HeaderSlider](./blocks/HeaderSlider.md) — Renders a carousel of full-bleed header-block slides — each slide carries its own title, description, buttons, and background media. Use it when the top of the page needs to rotate multiple equally important campaigns or announcements instead of a single hero.
166	- [Hero](./blocks/Hero.md) — Renders a modern, content-driven hero block: an overtitle, a rich content column (title, body text, list, links, buttons) and a media column (image/video/iframe) that adapts to its intrinsic aspect ratio. Use it as the primary landing block when you want more layout flexibility than the classic Header provides.
167	- [Icons](./blocks/Icons.md) — Renders a responsive grid of small icon items, each consisting of an image and a caption. Items can optionally be wrapped in links, turning the grid into a navigable set of icon links.
168	- [Info](./blocks/Info.md) — Renders a two-column information section: a left content column and a right content column, each with its own title, text, lists, buttons, and links, placed inside an optional themed background container.
169	- [Map](./blocks/Map.md) — A media-and-content block that embeds an interactive Yandex Map inside a card, paired with an optional title, description, links, and buttons.
170	- [Media](./blocks/Media.md) — Renders a two-column layout that pairs a content column (title, body, list, links, button) with a media column (image, video, YouTube, iframe, or DataLens embed). Use it for feature or explainer sections where text and a rich media asset need to sit side by side.
171	- [PromoFeaturesBlock](./blocks/PromoFeaturesBlock.md) — Renders a masonry layout of promotional feature cards, each pairing a title, YFM text, and an optional media asset, displayed against a full-width background. Use it for marketing sections that showcase several value propositions with rich imagery in a non-uniform grid.
172	- [Questions](./blocks/Questions.md) — Renders an FAQ block: a left content panel (title, text, links, buttons) and a list of expandable question/answer rows on the right. Automatically emits FAQPage JSON-LD microdata so search engines can index the answers as rich results.
173	- [Share](./blocks/Share.md) — Renders a row of social-network share buttons that share the current page URL.
174	- [Slider](./blocks/Slider.md) — A carousel block that renders any number of child cards as swipeable slides, with optional title, description, dots, arrows, autoplay, and per-breakpoint slide counts. Built on top of Swiper.
175	- [SliderOld](./blocks/SliderOld.md)
176	- [Table](./blocks/Table.md) — Renders a title followed by a comparison-style table whose cells are plain strings or numbers. A legend column can be marked with disk or tick markers, and an optional legend list explains the marked columns.
177	- [Tabs](./blocks/Tabs.md) — Renders a set of tab buttons that switch between rich content panels. Each tab panel pairs a content column (title, text, lists, buttons, links) with an optional media column (image, video, YouTube, iframe, DataLens), with control over column order, sizing, and border treatment.
178	
179	## Sub-blocks
180	
181	- [BackgroundCard](./sub-blocks/BackgroundCard.md) — A card that renders text content (title, text, links, buttons, or a content list) over a decorative background image or solid color. Useful for promotional cards inside a card layout.
182	- [BannerCard](./sub-blocks/BannerCard.md) — A compact banner card with a title, optional subtitle, a single call-to-action button, and a decorative background image. Designed to draw attention inside a card layout.
183	- [BasicCard](./sub-blocks/BasicCard.md) — A general-purpose card with an optional icon (image or Gravity UI icon) and text content (title, text, links, buttons, or a content list). The simplest and most versatile card.
184	- [Content](./sub-blocks/Content.md) — A text content block rendering a title, body text, additional info, links, buttons, and/or an icon content list. Used on its own as the textual portion of a content layout.

189	- [MediaCard](./sub-blocks/MediaCard.md) — Wraps a single media element (image, image slider, video, YouTube, iframe, or DataLens) inside a card with an optional border. Pure media card — no text content.
190	- [PriceCard](./sub-blocks/PriceCard.md) — Renders a pricing card: a title, a price (with optional period and details), a description, a checklist of features, and optional buttons and links. Typically placed in a grid to compare plans.
191	- [PriceDetailed](./sub-blocks/PriceDetailed.md)
192	- [Quote](./sub-blocks/Quote.md) — Renders a customer testimonial / quote card: a logo, the quote body, an optional author (name + avatar + description), and an optional CTA button. Paired with a large image on the side.

70	    <PageConstructorProvider>
71	      <PageConstructor content={content} />
72	    </PageConstructorProvider>
73	  );
74	};
75	
76	export default App;
77	```
78	
79	This was the simplest example of a connection. In order for YFM markup to work, you need to process content on the server and receive it on the client.
80	
81	If your server is a separate application, then you need to install page-constructor:
82	
83	```shell
84	npm install @gravity-ui/page-constructor
85	```
86	
87	To process YFM in all base blocks, call the `contentTransformer` and pass the content and options there:
88	
89	```ts
90	const express = require('express');
91	const app = express();
92	const {contentTransformer} = require('@gravity-ui/page-constructor/server');
93	
94	const content = {
95	  blocks: [
96	    {
97	      type: 'header-block',
98	      title: 'Hello world',
99	      background: {color: '#f0f0f0'},
100	      description:
101	        '**Congratulations!** Have you built a [page-constructor](https://github.com/gravity-ui/page-constructor) into your website',
102	    },
103	  ],
104	};
105	
106	app.get('/content', (req, res) => {
107	  res.send({content: contentTransformer({content, options: {lang: 'en'}})});
108	});
109	
110	app.listen(3000);
111	```
112	
113	On the client, add an endpoint call to receive content:
114	
115	```tsx
116	import {PageConstructor, PageConstructorProvider} from '@gravity-ui/page-constructor';
117	import '@gravity-ui/page-constructor/styles/styles.scss';
118	import {useEffect, useState} from 'react';
119	
120	const App = () => {
121	  const [content, setContent] = useState();
122	
123	  useEffect(() => {
124	    (async () => {
125	      const response = await fetch('http://localhost:3000/content').then((r) => r.json());
126	      setContent(response.content);
127	    })();
128	  }, []);
129	
130	  return (
131	    <PageConstructorProvider>
132	      <PageConstructor content={content} />
133	    </PageConstructorProvider>
134	  );
135	};
136	
137	export default App;
138	```

150	- [Data preparation](./guides/data-preparation.md) — This chapter provides documentaion for server utilities for transforming content, including Yandex Flavored Markdown (YFM) to HTML conversion and text processing. Key features include:
151	- [Подготовка данных](./guides/data-preparation-ru.md) — Документацию по серверным утилитам для преобразования контента, включая конвертацию Yandex Flavored Markdown (YFM) в HTML и обработку текста. Основные возможности:

153	## Blocks
154	
155	- [Banner](./blocks/Banner.md) — Renders a compact promotional card with a title, subtitle, an optional background image or color, and a single call-to-action button. Use it to highlight a feature, announce a release, or drive traffic to a landing page from anywhere in the page flow.
156	- [CardLayout](./blocks/CardLayout.md) — Renders a responsive grid of arbitrary cards (children) with an optional header and a decorative background image. 157	- [Companies](./blocks/Companies.md) — Renders a heading with a logo strip — a set of responsive images (desktop / tablet / mobile) shown beneath an optional title and description. Use it for "trusted by" or "powered by" logo rows that must adapt per device and theme.

Use it for documentation-style sections, terms, descriptions, or anywhere a focused block of text with file attachments is needed.
159	- [ExtendedFeatures](./blocks/ExtendedFeatures.md) — Renders a responsive grid of feature cards, each with an icon, title, text, an optional label (New / Preview), and an optional link. Use it to present a list of product features, capabilities, or benefits in a compact, icon-driven layout.

161	- [FoldableList](./blocks/FoldableList.md) — Renders a two-column block: a content panel on the left (title, text, links, buttons) and a list of collapsible items on the right, each with its own title, YFM text, and optional link. 162	- [Footer](./blocks/Footer.md) — A configurable page footer assembled from optional floors: navigation columns, contacts (social icons), disclaimer, copyright (legal links, language switcher, logo), and an attribution strip.

166	- [Hero](./blocks/Hero.md) — Renders a modern, content-driven hero block: an overtitle, a rich content column (title, body text, list, links, buttons) and a media column (image/video/iframe) that adapts to its intrinsic aspect ratio. 167	- [Icons](./blocks/Icons.md) — Renders a responsive grid of small icon items, each consisting of an image and a caption. Items can optionally be wrapped in links, turning the grid into a navigable set of icon links.

# Header

Renders a full-width page header with a title, optional overtitle/description, call-to-action buttons, breadcrumbs, and an optional media asset (image, video, or video iframe) positioned to the right or centered. Use it as the primary hero/landing block at the top of a page.

## Block type

`type: 'header-block'`

## When to use

- As the first block of a page to introduce the product, section, or campaign.
- When you need a large headline paired with CTA buttons and an illustration or background media.
- When you want breadcrumbs, status pills, or additional info alongside the title.

## Example

```json
{
  "type": "header-block",
  "title": "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit",
  "description": "**Ut enim ad minim veniam** [quis nostrud](https://example.com) exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat.",
  "additionalInfo": "**Ut enim ad minim veniam** ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat.",
  "buttons": [
    {"text": "Primary", "theme": "action", "url": "https://example.com"},
    {"text": "Secondary", "theme": "outlined", "url": "https://example.com"}
  ],
  "background": {
    "light": {"image": "/images/header-bg-light.png", "color": "#EFF2F8"},
    "dark": {"image": "/images/header-bg-dark.png", "color": "#262626"}
  }
}
```

## Properties

| Property           | Type                                                      | Default                | Description                                                                 |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title` _required_ | `string`                                                  | —                      | Main heading text (YFM-supported). Rendered as `<h1>`.                      |
| `overtitle`        | `string`                                                  | —                      | Small label rendered above the title. Accepts YFM or a React node.          |
| `description`      | `string`                                                  | —                      | YFM body text shown below the title.                                        |
| `additionalInfo`   | `string`                                                  | —                      | YFM supplementary text shown below the description.                         |
| `width`            | `'s' \| 'm' \| 'l'`                                       | `'m'`                  | Maximum text width; also drives the title size.                             |
| `buttons`          | `ButtonBlock[]`                                           | —                      | Call-to-action buttons rendered under the text.                             |
| `offset`           | `'default' \| 'large'`                                    | `'default'`            | Horizontal indent of the content column.                                    |
| `image`            | `ImageProps \| {light, dark}`                             | —                      | Inline media image placed on the right side.                                |
| `video`            | `VideoProps \| {light, dark}`                             | —                      | Inline media video placed on the right side.                                |
| `videoIframe`      | `{src, autoplay?, previewImg?, height?} \| {light, dark}` | —                      | External iframe video (e.g. video hosting) placed on the right side.        |
| `mediaView`        | `'fit' \| 'full'`                                         | `'full'`               | `fit` constrains the media height; `full` lets it fill the available space. |
| `backLink`         | `{url, title}`                                            | —                      | "Back" navigation link rendered above the title.                            |
| `imageSize`        | `'s' \| 'm'`                                              | derived from `width`   | Overrides the inline media column size.                                     |
| `verticalOffset`   | `'0' \| 's' \| 'm' \| 'l' \| 'xl'`                        | `'m'`                  | Vertical spacing around the content.                                        |
| `background`       | `HeaderBackgroundProps \| {light, dark}`                  | —                      | Full-bleed background media/color behind the content.                       |
| `theme`            | `'default' \| 'dark'`                                     | `'light'` (text theme) | Text/background color scheme for the content area.                          |
| `breadcrumbs`      | `{items: {url, text}[], theme?}`                          | —                      | Breadcrumb navigation rendered above the content.                           |
| `status`           | `string`                                                  | —                      | Status text/React node rendered next to the title.                          |
| `centered`         | `boolean`                                                 | `false`                | Centers the content and hides the right-side media.                         |

`HeaderBackgroundProps` extends `MediaProps` with `fullWidth?: boolean` and `fullWidthMedia?: boolean`.

### Common properties

Inherits common block properties: `anchor`, `visible`, `indent` (`{top?, bottom?}`), `qa`, `className`, `animated`, `theme` (`'light' | 'dark'`), `when`, `context`. See the root README for details.

## Themed values

`image`, `video`, `videoIframe`, and `background` each accept either a plain value or a `{light, dark}` object resolved against the active runtime theme.

## Storybook

[Header](https://preview.gravity-ui.com/page-constructor/?path=/docs/blocks-header--docs)
# ExtendedFeatures

Renders a responsive grid of feature cards, each with an icon, title, text, an optional label (`New` / `Preview`), and an optional link. Use it to present a list of product features, capabilities, or benefits in a compact, icon-driven layout.

## Block type

`type: 'extended-features-block'`

## When to use

- Showcasing a set of features or capabilities with a small icon each.
- Highlighting new or preview items via a built-in `New` / `Preview` label.
- When you need per-item links to documentation or landing pages.

## Example

```json

  "type": "extended-features-block",
  "title": {"text": "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet"},
  "description": "Three **cards in a row on the desktop**, two cards in a row on a tablet, one card in a row on a mobile phone.",
  "items": [
    {
      "title": "Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt",
      "text": "Ut enim ad minim veniam [quis nostrud](https://example.com) ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat.",
      "icon": {"light": "/story-assets/icon_1_light.svg", "dark": "/story-assets/icon_1_dark.svg"}
    },
    {
      "title": "Sed do eiusmod tempor",
      "text": "Ut enim ad minim veniam [quis nostrud](https://example.com) ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat.",
      "icon": {"light": "/story-assets/icon_2_light.svg", "dark": "/story-assets/icon_2_dark.svg"},
      "label": "New"
    },
    {
      "title": "Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt",
      "text": "Ut enim ad minim veniam [quis nostrud](https://example.com) ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat.",
      "icon": {"light": "/story-assets/icon_3_light.svg", "dark": "/story-assets/icon_3_dark.svg"},
      "link": {"text": "Go", "url": "#", "arrow": true, "theme": "normal"}
    }
  ]
}
```

## Properties

| Property      | Type                                              | Default                   | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`       | `string \| TitleProps`                            | —                         | Block heading (string or Title options). |
| `description` | `string`                                          | —                         | YFM subtitle shown under the title.                                                                 |
| `items`       | `ExtendedFeaturesItem[]`                          | —                         | Array of feature cards (see below).                                                                 |
| `colSizes`    | `{all?, sm?, md?, lg?, xl?}` (each `number` 1–12) | `{all: 12, sm: 6, md: 4}` | Column width per breakpoint for a single feature.                                                   |
| `animated`    | `boolean`                                         | —                         | Enables entrance animation for the block.                                                           |

### `ExtendedFeaturesItem`

| Property | Type                          | Default | Description                                                                     |
| -------- | ----------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`  | `string`                      | —       | Feature title. Rendered as `<h3>` when the block has a title, otherwise `<h2>`. |
| `text`   | `string`                      | —       | YFM body text.                                                                  |
| `label`  | `'New' \| 'Preview'`          | —       | Small badge rendered next to the title.                                         |
| `link`   | `LinkProps`                   | —       | Single link rendered below the text.                                            |
| `icon`   | `ImageProps \| {light, dark}` | —       | Icon image shown above the title.                                               |

### Common properties

Inherits common block properties: `anchor`, `visible`, `indent` (`{top?, bottom?}`), `qa`, `className`, `animated`, `theme` (`'light' | 'dark'`), `when`, `context`. See the root README for details.

## Themed values

`icon` accepts either a plain value or a `{light, dark}` object resolved against the active runtime theme.

## Storybook

[ExtendedFeatures](https://preview.gravity-ui.com/page-constructor/?path=/docs/blocks-extendedfeatures--docs)
# Banner

Renders a compact promotional card with a title, subtitle, an optional background image or color, and a single call-to-action button. Use it to highlight a feature, announce a release, or drive traffic to a landing page from anywhere in the page flow.

## Block type

`type: 'banner-block'`

## When to use

- Mid-page promotional card with a clear single CTA.
- When you need a compact, image-rich block that fits alongside other content.
- As a stand-alone banner or as a card inside grid-based layouts (also registered as `banner-card`).

## Example

```json
{
  "type": "banner-block",
  "title": "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit",
